history.dynasty: None (modern; built by the JK Trust / Singhania family, Juggilal Kamlapat Organisation)
history.period: JK Trust formed 1953; construction completed 20 May 1960 (some sources loosely say 'built in 1953')
history.summary: The JK Temple (officially Shri Radhakrishna Temple), a modern Hindu temple in Sarvodaya Nagar, Kanpur, built by the JK Trust of the Singhania family on a 17-acre campus (per the official site). It is known for blending ancient and modern architecture, with five shrines: the central Shri Radhakrishna shrine plus Lakshminarayan, Ardhanarishwar, Narmadeshwar and Hanuman, plus a lake and landscaped gardens. Note: the geocoder could not match the temple POI exactly, so the coordinates are approximate to Sarvodaya Nagar Road; opening hours differ across sources (5:00-12:00 & 4:30/4:00 PM-10:00/9:00 PM) - verify.

name: JK Temple (Shri Radhakrishna Temple)
town_description: Kanpur is Uttar Pradesh's major industrial city on the south bank of the Ganga, about 80 km west of Lucknow. Once called the 'Manchester of the East', it is today a large commercial and educational centre with several prominent temples.

travel.airport: Kanpur Airport (~14 km); Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, Lucknow (~70 km)
travel.road: Sarvodaya Nagar, Kanpur; reachable by taxi and auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (Janmashtami in August is the liveliest festival)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 4:30 PM - 10:00 PM (sources differ; verify)
